obs: United States Ex Rel. Steinmetz v. Allen
"A ruling having such effect must be considered as final and appealable."
Switchmen's Union v. National Mediation Board

"Where an Act fails to provide for review of preliminary rulings determining status in preparation for subsequent action, or performing administrative duties which were not final in character, such rulings have not been considered as subject to review by virtue of general statutory review provisions. The reason that review is not allowed at such a stage is that the rulings or orders are only preparation for future effective action."
"Judicial review of such a preliminary step in a judicial proceeding is so unique that we are not willing easily to infer that it exists."
Federal Trade Commission v. Standard Oil Co.
“[t]he cases dealing with judicial review of administrative actions have interpreted the ‘finality’ element in a pragmatic way.”
“The strong presumption is that judicial review will be available only when agency action becomes final … and there is nothing in 455 to overcome that presumption.”
“Our cases have interpreted pragmatically the requirement of administrative finality, focusing on whether judicial review at the time will disrupt the administrative process.”
